sections.heading: C — Vehicle failures, communicating risk, collisions, power lines and traffic stops
sections.markdown:
## C — Vehicle failures, communicating risk, collisions, power lines and traffic stops

FACT_ID: sec14-F01 | anchor: A173
When your vehicle has trouble, get it off the road if you can, or stop where others can see it clearly, never just past a hilltop or around a curve. [A173]
Source: [A173 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0173]

FACT_ID: sec14-F02 | anchor: A173
For a breakdown, switch on your emergency flashers and headlights and set flares 200 to 300 feet behind the vehicle. [A173]
Source: [A173 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0173]

FACT_ID: sec14-F03 | anchor: A173
Without flares, stand somewhere safe and wave traffic around, and signal an emergency by raising the hood or tying a white cloth to the antenna, mirror or door handle. [A173]
Source: [A173 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0173]

FACT_ID: sec14-F04 | anchor: A173
If a tire blows out, grip the wheel firmly, keep going straight, lift off the accelerator and let the car slow on its own, braking only gently if needed. [A173]
Why it matters: the instinct to brake hard is exactly what the guide says not to do.
Source: [A173 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0173]

FACT_ID: sec14-F05 | anchor: A173
If you cannot reach a safe spot to change a flat, turn on hazard lights, stay inside the vehicle and call for help. [A173]
Source: [A173 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0173]

FACT_ID: sec14-F06 | anchor: A174
If the engine dies while driving, hold the wheel firmly, since steering gets harder but still works, and brake with steady pressure rather than hard while you pull off. [A174]
Source: [A174 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0174]

FACT_ID: sec14-F07 | anchor: A174
After the engine dies and you stop, try a restart, and if it fails raise the hood, turn on hazard lights and call for help. [A174]
Source: [A174 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0174]

FACT_ID: sec14-F08 | anchor: A174
If your headlights suddenly fail, turn on hazard lights, turn signals or fog lights if you have them and leave the road as soon as you can. [A174]
Source: [A174 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0174]

FACT_ID: sec14-F09 | anchor: A174
If the accelerator sticks and the car keeps speeding up, keep your eyes on the road, shift quickly to neutral, pull off when safe and turn off the engine. [A174]
Source: [A174 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0174]

FACT_ID: sec14-F10 | anchor: A174
Your lights, horn and hand signals are the tools for warning other road users that a risk is present. [A174]
Source: [A174 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0174]

FACT_ID: sec14-F11 | anchor: A175
Every driver is responsible for preventing crashes, which can call for evasive moves, yet even a good driver can still end up in a collision. [A175]
Source: [A175 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0175]

FACT_ID: sec14-F12 | anchor: A175
The guide names three usual causes of collisions: too much speed, too little space and poor situational awareness. [A175]
Source: [A175 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0175]

FACT_ID: sec14-F13 | anchor: A175
After a crash, never drive away, and if anyone is hurt or killed, call 911 because police must be notified. [A175]
Source: [A175 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0175]

FACT_ID: sec14-F14 | anchor: A175
Move a crashed vehicle to the roadside close to the collision site as soon as you can, and stay out of the traffic lanes. [A175]
Source: [A175 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0175]

FACT_ID: sec14-F15 | anchor: A176
At a crash, warn others with flares or other devices, switch off the wrecked vehicles, and do not smoke because spilled fuel can catch fire. [A176]
Source: [A176 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0176]

FACT_ID: sec14-F16 | anchor: A176
If you hit a parked vehicle you must try to find the owner, and if you cannot, leave a visible note with the date, time and your contact details. [A176]
Source: [A176 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0176]

FACT_ID: sec14-F17 | anchor: A176
Drivers in a crash exchange names, contact details, driver license numbers, insurance companies and policy numbers, and should photograph the damage. [A176]
Source: [A176 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0176]

FACT_ID: sec14-F18 | anchor: A176
State law requires you to file a collision report form within 4 days of a crash when a police officer does not file one for you. [A176]
Source: [A176 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0176]

FACT_ID: sec14-F19 | anchor: A176
Do not move injured people unless they are in a burning vehicle or other immediate danger. [A176]
Source: [A176 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0176]

FACT_ID: sec14-F20 | anchor: A177
Help anyone who is not walking and talking by checking breathing first and then bleeding. [A177]
Source: [A177 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0177]

FACT_ID: sec14-F21 | anchor: A177
For bleeding the guide lists hand pressure first, then a bandage or dressing, then a tourniquet. [A177]
Source: [A177 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0177]

FACT_ID: sec14-F22 | anchor: A177
Give injured people nothing to drink, not even water, and cover them with a blanket or coat to keep them warm and help prevent shock. [A177]
Source: [A177 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0177]

FACT_ID: sec14-F23 | anchor: A177
On a 911 call, stay calm and give your location with nearby landmarks or mile markers, then briefly describe the vehicles, damage and injuries. [A177]
Source: [A177 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0177]

FACT_ID: sec14-F24 | anchor: A178
Stay on the line with the 911 dispatcher until help arrives, ready to add details such as vehicle types, plate numbers and hazards. [A178]
Source: [A178 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0178]

FACT_ID: sec14-F25 | anchor: A178
If a power line touches your vehicle, do not get out; turn off the engine, call 911 and wait inside for responders, treating every line as live. [A178]
Source: [A178 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0178]

FACT_ID: sec14-F26 | anchor: A178
If you drive over a power line, stop at once, because moving forward or backing up risks electrocution, and stay inside until told it is safe. [A178]
Source: [A178 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0178]

FACT_ID: sec14-F27 | anchor: A178
When lines fall on your vehicle or you hit a transformer box, the ground nearby may be energized, so urge people to stay at least 35 feet away. [A178]
Source: [A178 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0178]

FACT_ID: sec14-F28 | anchor: A178
If fire starts while a power line touches your vehicle, jump clear with arms at your sides and both feet landing together, without touching the vehicle, then shuffle 35 feet away. [A178]
Why it matters: fire is the only case where the guide tells you to leave a vehicle touched by a power line.
Source: [A178 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0178]

FACT_ID: sec14-F29 | anchor: A179
Passing a crash, do not block responders, obey anyone authorized to direct traffic there, and keep your eyes on driving because slowing to stare causes congestion. [A179]
Source: [A179 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0179]

FACT_ID: sec14-F30 | anchor: A179
A vehicle emergency kit can hold a first aid kit, flashlight, blanket, water, jumper cables, tools, a backup charger, spare tire and jack, and reflective triangles or flares. [A179]
Source: [A179 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0179]

FACT_ID: sec14-F31 | anchor: A179
Keep a paper list of important phone numbers in case your phone dies and you must call from another phone. [A179]
Source: [A179 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0179]

FACT_ID: sec14-F32 | anchor: A180
Police signal a stop with flashing lights, a siren or both, and you respond by signaling and pulling to the right side of the road as soon as it is safe. [A180]
Source: [A180 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0180]

FACT_ID: sec14-F33 | anchor: A180
Once stopped for police, turn off the engine and any radio or audio, and stay in the vehicle unless the officer tells you to get out. [A180]
Source: [A180 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0180]

FACT_ID: sec14-F34 | anchor: A181
At a night stop turn on your interior lights, keep your hands on the wheel, and follow all instructions given to you or your passengers. [A181]
Source: [A181 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0181]

FACT_ID: sec14-F35 | anchor: A181
When the officer comes up, lower the window on that side, say right away if a weapon is in the vehicle, and wait for instructions before reaching for documents. [A181]
Source: [A181 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0181]

FACT_ID: sec14-F36 | anchor: A181
An officer will usually ask for your driver license, proof of insurance and vehicle registration, so say where they are before you reach for them. [A181]
Source: [A181 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0181]

FACT_ID: sec14-F37 | anchor: A182
You may respectfully ask the officer questions, but if you disagree, do not argue; you can contest the decision in court or contact the officer's agency to ask for a supervisor. [A182]
Source: [A182 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0182]

FACT_ID: sec14-F38 | anchor: A182
You must sign a traffic ticket, signing does not admit guilt, and refusing to sign can lead to arrest. [A182]
Source: [A182 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0182]

FACT_ID: sec14-F39 | anchor: A182
Follow the instructions on the back of a ticket within 15 days or your driving privileges can be suspended. [A182]
Source: [A182 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0182]

Glossary: emergency flashers — the hazard warning lights [A173]. Collision report form — the state crash report a driver files when police do not [A176]. Tourniquet — a band tightened to stop severe bleeding, listed last among the bleeding steps [A177]. Energized — carrying electric current [A178].
Memory aid: at a power line, stay in unless fire, then jump, land together and shuffle away [A178].
